## Historical cleanup source sorting and qualification

The following cleanup retirement, archive, unit and gate records describe sealed cleanup69b39630; they are preserved historical evidence, not a claim that the new merge ports have passed.


There are 611 original source paths absent from this commit: 50 current-version class-2 paths and 561 class-3 paths. They are distinct from the 72 literal historical producer versions archived with retained-result bindings. The full deletion table is included below and in REMOVED.md, including source line counts, Git history and Studio actions. No scientific DATA, result or partial output was deleted.

The prior candidate passed 445 unit tests; its final Studio gate exposed nine deferred imports to relocated saved readers. Those routes are corrected without changing numerical functions, and nine behavioral route/guard regressions passed. The full suite and final gates are recorded separately for this commit. The three mandatory tests and qualified CUDA provider are byte-unchanged. All 24 substantive duplicate families resolve to one canonical implementation. The final numerical/Studio gates and G4/G6 receipts are separate immutable reports bound to this commit.

The integrated candidate passed 538 unit tests, including 84 new cases (82 public-API contracts and two runtime-documentation contracts). All 398 public method-core APIs were observed in passed cases by a source-bound Python call profile. The CUDA cases used actual available CuPy for 14 small float32/float64 GPU tests; missing-device skips would not count as passed API calls. This is unit evidence, not a new scientific equivalence qualification or throughput benchmark. The final clean-commit gate report separately records numerical and Studio qualification.

The provider file retains its exact original bytes and 23 raw AST docstring slots remain None. The mass package initializer attaches physical-purpose and parameter runtime __doc__ text to those same function objects without altering co_code/co_consts, signatures or the two existing in-file docs. All 25 CUDA public methods therefore have runtime help strings; a fresh CPU import loads no CuPy or device allocation. This is runtime documentation, not a claim that literal strings were inserted into the byte-locked file.
